description: Renovate configuration for the homelab GitOps monorepo.
Renovate runs SELF-HOSTED as a CronJob in the cluster (see
infrastructure/controllers/renovate/README.md) and reads this file from the
default branch. Renovate only ever opens pull requests -- nothing reaches the
cluster until a human merges to main and Flux reconciles the merge commit.
Native Flux manager: bumps spec.chart.spec.version in HelmRelease objects
(resolved through the HelmRepository/OCIRepository objects in
infrastructure/sources/), GitRepository tags, and docker images referenced
inside HelmRelease .spec.values. The default pattern only covers
gotk-components.yaml, so it is widened to the whole monorepo here.
Plain Kubernetes manifests: image tags in Deployments, StatefulSets,
DaemonSets and CronJobs -- including Renovate's own CronJob image.

github-actions.description: CI workflows owned by topic 3 (lint.yaml, test.yaml, build-images.yaml).

dockerfile.description: Base images of the webapp container builds owned by topic 4.

pip_requirements.description: Django/aioquic/Hypercorn pins of the webapp backend.

description: CROSS-TOPIC CONTRACT (PLAN.md section 4.6): the webapp's OWN images are
promoted by Flux image automation (ImageRepository/ImagePolicy/
ImageUpdateAutomation in apps/base/webapp/). If Renovate also proposed tags
for them the two automations would fight -- Flux commits a new tag directly
to main, Renovate would open a PR reverting/duplicating it. Renovate owns
THIRD-PARTY dependencies only.
Patch updates are grouped into ONE PR and automerged.
Why patch-only automerge: patch releases are, by semver contract,
backwards-compatible bug/security fixes; reviewing ~20 of them a month by
hand is busywork that leads to rubber-stamping. Minor and major updates can
change defaults, CRDs or chart values and therefore always wait for a human.
Guard rails: minimumReleaseAge gives the ecosystem 3 days to yank a bad
release, and platformAutomerge means GitHub only merges after the required
CI checks (topic 3's lint/test workflows) pass. Patch and minor are two
SEPARATE groups on purpose: a mixed group would take the highest update
type (minor) and would therefore never automerge.

packageRules.description: Minor updates: one grouped PR per run, reviewed and merged by a human.

description: Major updates always get their own PR with a changelog to read, never
automerged -- these are the ones that break CRDs and chart values.
Helm charts that install CRDs (Linkerd, cert-manager, ARC,
kube-prometheus-stack) are never grouped with anything else, even for
minor bumps: a chart minor can ship a CRD schema change that must be rolled
out in its own reconciliation.
Renovate updating its own CronJob image -- the bootstrap loop. Kept out of
the grouped PRs so a broken Renovate release is trivial to revert.
Digest-only churn (third-party image digests, plus the GitHub Action SHAs
pinned by helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests) is grouped into one PR and
automerged: a digest bump for an unchanged tag carries no API change, and
reviewing SHAs by hand is impossible anyway.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the daily window and are never automerged.
